narration.text: Every clinician's Medicare revalidation, credentialing attestation and license kept current, on four clocks in four portals. This is a chore for the credentialing coordinator of a family clinic with four clinicians and a DMEPOS supplier enrollment for the braces and crutches it dispenses. Read the credentialing folder: each clinician's liability certificates, CME transcripts and the separation notice of a physician who left. Athena works it across 4 portals: Docshelf, Enrollpoint, Credvault and Boardline. On the bench, she found 8 of 8 eligible items, worth 1,200 dollars of the 1,200 dollars there was to find. She made no false claim. The world held 10 traps, and she walked past 10. Among them: A revalidation whose due date is TBD. A revalidation due in more than seven months. She took 3 minutes. By hand, the same chore takes 2 hours, so she was about 46 times faster. The verdict: exceeds. She beat the bar this playbook set itself. The bar was 75 percent of the money, no false claim and inside 60 minutes. Every card she filed waited for a person's signature, and nothing was sent.
